text:
maya: heads up — ran into a merge blocker for a docs-only PR. CODEOWNERS required a review from eng infra but CI has an unrelated failing check (lint:js-runtime) that doesn't touch docs. can we make docs-only PRs skip that check? :thinking:

sam: yeah i've seen this. GitHub branch protection enforces required status checks for all PRs, there's no path-based ignore there by default. but our Actions workflows can use `paths`/`paths-ignore` to avoid running things on docs changes. which workflow is causing the lint check?

maya: it's the monorepo `ci.yml` that runs the full test matrix. PR is just `docs/v1/migration.md` + tiny markdown tweaks. Ideally we don't run JS lint or unit tests for pure docs.

sam: easiest is to split the workflows: make a docs-only workflow and set `paths: ["docs/**"]` so the heavy jobs never kick off. then update the branch protection to require the lightweight `docs-preview` check only for docs changes. but branch protection can't be conditional on paths. you'd need two things: 1) ensure heavy checks don't run on docs-only PRs, 2) have a docs-specific status check that is allowed to be required.

neil: other option is to add a short presubmit that detects docs-only and posts a `status check` named `docs-only` via the GitHub Checks API or a lightweight action. Then make that check required in branch protection. Workflow idea: 
```yaml
name: docs-sentinel
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  detect:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: detect docs-only
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          git diff --name-only origin/${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}...HEAD > changed.txt
          if grep -qvE "^(docs/|README.md)$" changed.txt; then echo "non-docs" && exit 1; fi
      - name: create-check
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          script: "github.checks.create({owner: context.repo.owner, repo: context.repo.repo, name: 'docs-sentinel', head_sha: context.payload.pull_request.head.sha, status: 'completed', conclusion: 'success'})"
```

jen: sounds reasonable. question: who owns the CODEOWNERS rules? right now docs/* maps to `@docs` and infra/* maps to `@eng-infra`. The blocker is CODEOWNERS also triggers required reviewer requests — but that shouldn't block merge if review approvals are satisfied. Are approvals the actual blocker or the failing status check?

maya: approvals were fine — the PR had two docs reviewers. GitHub prevented merge because `lint:js-runtime` failed.

sam: ok then we definitely need to not run that lint on docs-only PRs. quick patch: in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` wrap the lint job with: `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && contains(github.event.pull_request.changed_files, 'docs/')` — hmm, `changed_files` isn't exposed like that. Better to use the `paths` filter at the top-level job or rely on the detect job above.

neil: alternative: use `paths-ignore` on the heavy workflow: `paths-ignore: [ 'docs/**', 'README.md' ]` — that will skip the entire workflow when only docs are changed. safe and simple.

jen: any downsides? e.g., if someone edits a docs file plus a small code sample in a JS file, will the skip false-negative? no, `paths-ignore` only skips when all changed files match the ignore. so if there's any non-doc file changed, the heavy workflow runs — that's what we want.

maya: ok i'll open a tiny PR to add `paths-ignore` to the heavy workflow and a separate `docs-preview.yml` that runs the docs preview build and reports a `docs-preview` status check.

sam: also consider updating CODEOWNERS: currently `docs/**` lists `@docs-team` which requests reviews; but we want that to stay. just make sure branch protection doesn't force the heavy job.

neil: last point — auto-merge: GitHub auto-merge requires all required checks to pass before merging, and it won't override CODEOWNERS approvals. If you want auto-merge for docs-only PRs, set the required checks to include only the lightweight `docs-preview` check and allow auto-merge for PRs with `docs-only` label. We have a small probot that can apply the label based on changed files.

maya: perfect. do we need an owner to review the workflow PR? tagging @sam @neil for review. i'll also include a short test PR to verify behavior.

sam: ack, will review. once merged we should announce in #eng to avoid surprises. :loud_sound:

buildbot: build queued for branch: maya/docs-ci-skip (no heavy jobs triggered due to paths-ignore) :white_check_mark: 

maya: thanks everyone — i'll follow up with the PR link in this thread when ready. :+1:
